charts.title: Gross Profit, Operating Income & Net Income
EPS (statutory) & Dividend per Share
charts.annotation: FY2026 statutory EPS (2.0c) includes a A$63.1m BTP discontinued-operations loss; continuing diluted EPS was 8.6c. See the KPI cards above and the Profit lines chart's help for the full bridge.

charts.title: Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Perenti Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Perenti Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Perenti Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Perenti Limited: the bar chart plots statutory diluted EPS, which is why FY2026 collapses to 2.0c even though the business had a record year. Perenti reclassified its BTP subsidiary as discontinued operations in FY2026 pending an October-2026 sale; that reclassification alone books a A$63.1m non-cash loss below the continuing-operations line. Strip it out and continuing diluted EPS was 8.6c — a P/E of ~10.4x on underlying NPAT(A) of A$192.1m, not the 214x the statutory number implies. The KPI cards above show both figures side by side.

What to watch:

  • Whether the BTP sale completes on schedule (proceeds land in the DCF's cash bridge, not its flows)
  • Statutory EPS re-converging with continuing EPS once the discontinued-ops noise drops out of FY2027 comparatives
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Perenti Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Perenti Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Perenti Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Perenti Limited: the FY2026 net-income bar (A$18.8m) understates the year badly on its own: operating income held up (A$238.9m) while statutory net income fell 84% on two items below the operating line — a A$63.1m non-cash loss from reclassifying BTP as discontinued (sale completes Oct-2026) and A$54.3m of impairments on AMS Surface and idoba. Underlying NPAT(A), which excludes both, was A$192.1m, up 7.6% on FY2025.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs) — FY2026 is the extreme case

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Perenti Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Perenti Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue

dcf.base_sublabel: Owner FCF — after SBC, interest income & leases
dcf.model_approach_note: No rebuild required: diagnosis is statutory-EPS-only. The base case was already built on mid-cycle margins (FY20-26 average 17.5% EBITDA, gliding down from the FY26 record 18.3%), not peak-year FCF extrapolation, with a 12x owner-FCF terminal cap and a 30% bear weight already in place. The tripped P/E (214x) uses FY26 STATUTORY diluted EPS (2.0c), which carries a A.1m BTP discontinued-operations loss and A.3m of non-cash impairments -- both one-off, both already excluded from the forward flows. On FY26 underlying NPAT(A) (20c/share) the implied P/E is ~10.4x, inside the FY19-FY25 historical range of 6.7-15.2x. The other three multiples (EV/EBITDA 4.1x vs 3.3x avg/4.4x max, P/B 1.10x vs 1.11x max, P/Sales 0.60x vs 0.73x max) were already inside range and did not trip. No WACC premium was added on top, since cyclicality and African-policy risk are already charged once, in the bear flows and the 30% bear weight.
